profile.name: Carl Boyanton
profile.bio: Carl Boyanton owns a produce store and is running as an independent from the Gulfport area. He ran for this seat as a Republican in 2020, 2022 and 2024. He describes himself as a principled conservative alternative to both major parties.

platform.point: Targets fraud, waste and improper payments and warns about the rising national debt and interest costs.
Supports congressional term limits to reduce the influence of career politicians.
Says life begins at conception and abortion should be banned except in rare circumstances.
Backs border security and reform that puts citizens and legal residents first.
Wants schools focused on core subjects rather than what he calls divisive ideologies.
Argues both major parties protect the status quo and shut out outside challengers.

economy.evidence: Focuses on cutting federal waste and reducing debt and spending.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: would prohibit it except in exceptional circumstances; no stated positions on other issues.

immigration.evidence: Calls for border security and immigration policy that prioritizes citizens and legal residents.

profile.notes: The campaign image may be a graphic that includes his photo rather than a plain headshot.

profile.name: Kimberly Persico
profile.bio: Kimberly Persico, of Hot Springs, Montana, previously worked as an analytical chemist and math instructor in Wisconsin. In Montana she has worked in ranching, at a stockyard and veterinary clinic, and as a school paraprofessional, and founded an environmental consulting firm serving mining operations. She is running as a self-described conservative independent.

platform.point: Supports congressional term limits and the Transparent Election Initiative to limit election spending.
Wants to address the federal fiscal imbalance.
Put ordinary people ahead of large corporations and billionaires.
Protect public lands and support agriculture.

profile.notes: The campaign site cited on Wikipedia (keepingamericaspromise.com) currently redirects to a WordPress error page. Her stated themes are too general to score.

profile.name: Patrick McCracken
profile.bio: Patrick McCracken is the Libertarian nominee for Montana's 2nd congressional district. A lifelong Montanan from Columbia Falls, he has worked for about ten years as a financial advisor.

platform.point: Proposes the Send Baron Act to draft children of the president, cabinet and Congress first in any war.
Keep Medicaid expansion to sustain rural hospitals and pass the PRICE Transparency Act.
Treats housing costs as a monetary problem and backs breaking up private equity ownership of single-family homes.
Co-sponsor the American Beef Labeling Act for country-of-origin labeling.
Codify a ratepayer protection pledge for data center energy agreements and pursue cannabis banking reform.

economy.evidence: Opposes institutional investors buying single-family homes and backs mandatory beef origin labeling and ratepayer protections.

welfare.evidence: Calls Medicaid expansion essential to keeping rural Montana health care open.

profile.notes: No campaign website was found; positions come from Montana Free Press and Montana Public Radio questionnaires.

profile.name: Michael Eisenhauer
profile.bio: Michael Eisenhauer is an independent candidate for Montana's 2nd congressional district from Great Falls. He is a practicing interventional cardiologist and a retired Army colonel who served 25 years and received the Bronze Star. He qualified for the ballot by petition.

platform.point: Enforce and strengthen the War Powers Resolution so no branch acts alone on war.
Stabilise rural and critical-access hospitals, protect pre-existing condition coverage and patient choice without single-payer.
Transferable mortgages, development tax incentives, down-payment help, property tax relief and lower tariffs on building materials.
Enforce antitrust law, limit foreign corporate land purchases and return tariff authority to Congress.
Back the Transparent Election Initiative to curb dark money.

economy.evidence: Mixes antitrust enforcement and foreign land limits with tax incentives and lower tariffs.

welfare.evidence: Opposes single-payer health care while protecting pre-existing condition coverage and rural hospitals.

profile.notes: Campaign materials also use the name Mike Eisenhauer.

profile.name: Tom Bailey
profile.bio: Tom Bailey is the Libertarian nominee for North Carolina's 1st District. He works as a contractor and formerly chaired the Guilford County Libertarian Party. He has run for office several times before.
profile.notes: No campaign website or published issue positions were found; biographical details come from the Wikipedia page on the 2026 North Carolina House elections.

profile.name: Travis Groo
profile.bio: Travis Groo is a safety specialist and a former executive committee member of the Wake County Libertarian Party. He has run for office several times before and is the Libertarian nominee for North Carolina's 11th congressional district.

profile.name: Steven Swinton
profile.bio: Steven Swinton is a businessman and the Libertarian nominee for North Carolina's 13th congressional district. He was the Libertarian nominee for North Carolina's 19th Senate district in 2024.

profile.name: Daniel Cavender
